validation.notes: Regressions repaired in all three listed modules: (1) packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts - recoverToolInvocation had a dead `false &&` guard that made the non-cancelled safe/safe replay branch unreachable, so every recovery fell back to the interrupted checkpoint outcome; the guard is removed and the policy condition (not cancelled, persisted replay==='safe', declared tool replay==='safe') is evaluated again. (2) packages/agent/src/harness/execution/tools.ts - finalizeToolCall merged the after-tool patch with `patch?.isError || executed.isError`, which discarded an explicit `isError: false`; it now uses `??` so explicit false/empty patch values win while omitted values fall back to the executed result, and unspecified content/details/usage/terminate plus extra result keys are preserved. (3) packages/agent/src/harness/execution/effect-gate.ts - close() returned early for any non-open gate, so a terminal error could not supersede a pending cancellation; close now transitions an aborting gate to closed (only an already closed gate is ignored) and records the terminal error as the authoritative admission failure and abort reason, which a later beginAbort/close cannot downgrade. The regression script links the real modules through the read-only subject helper (only checkpoint storage, progress transport, hook delivery and provider imports are faked) and asserts with uncaught node:assert/strict: gate admission/AbortRequested/terminal-closure precedence, explicit isError=false with empty content and preserved details+usage, safe/safe replay invoking the tool with the persisted arguments and emitting no interruption marker, cancelled/never/never-persisted/missing-tool recoveries staying on the checkpoint path, progress update+checkpoint ordering, closed gate rejecting a replay with the terminal error, abort-wins admission not replaying, and mid-invocation gate closure making the terminal error authoritative. Local fixtures were created under a temporary directory inside .prale-eval/ and removed in a finally block. Mutation check: restoring each of the three modules individually to its faulty baseline (`false &&` guard, `||` isError merge, `close` ignoring aborting state) makes the same script exit non-zero with an AssertionError (verified for each file, never a crash/import error/timeout); with all fixes in place the script exits 0. No real time, randomness or external services are used as evidence; asynchronous ordering is promise-driven. Limitation: repository Vitest/TypeScript toolchains are not installed in this workspace (no node_modules and dependency installation is not permitted), so this harness script is the only executed validation; no tsc/vitest run was possible.
